title: Add cell selection functionality to `st.dataframe`
body:
### Problem

In the official tutorial about [`st.dataframe`](https://<redacted-host>/library/api-reference/data/st.dataframe#interactivity), it provides a well interactive UI, but it lacks one important feature: **indicate the selected `(row, column)`**.

For example:

```py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame(
   np.random.randn(50, 20),
   columns=('col %d' % i for i in range(20)))

st.dataframe(df)
```

We can change the last line to the following:

```py
row, column = st.dataframe(df)
```

And we can select a specific cell in the GUI:

![Screenshot 2023-06-02 at 21 17 16](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/804308/adeed4cd-3778-4fdb-a294-bb97cfa0ca08)

Now we can do something with the selected row and/or column (in the above case: `row==4` and `column=="col 2"`). For example, we can show the detail info for the selected row.

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

![Views](https://<redacted-host>/badge/st-issue-6781)

comments.body:
# Update

Hey all! Thanks for all the upvotes and comments. We released row and column selections for dataframes in 1.35 (see [here](https://<redacted-host>/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe#dataframe-selections)). 

The reason we haven't touched cell selections yet is that clicking a cell is used for a bunch of other operations in our current dataframe implementation (e.g. viewing the unformatted value of a cell, viewing long values of cells, copy pasting, editing in `st.data_editor` etc). Simply adding cell selections on top of that would not be a great UX since it would collapse with all these other features. E.g. imagine you have a long text cell and want to see the entire text, and that causes the cell selection to trigger. Before we implement cell selections, we probably want to revisit the UX of our dataframe implementation and adjust a few things to have fewer conflicts. 

We don't have a timeline for that yet, but please keep upvoting and describing your use cases, that helps us a lot in prioritizing this versus other features!

comments.body:
## Update

Single- and multi-cell selection for `st.dataframe` will be released in 1.49:

```python
selection = st.dataframe(df, on_select="rerun", selection_mode="single-cell")
st.write("Dataframe single-cell selection:", selection)
```

It can also be combined with other selection modes:

```python
selection = st.dataframe(df, on_select="rerun", selection_mode=("multi-row", "multi-cell"))

for row, col in selection["selection"]["cells"]:
    st.write(f"Selected cell: {row}, {col}")
```


Thanks to @participant7 implementing this more than a year ago and keeping the branch up-to-date.
